To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of uneven surface topography on macrosegregation in aluminum alloys solidifying from uneven surfaces depends on amplitude and wavelength.

(1) In the vertical configuration, inverse segregation occurs in the bottom of the cavity and is enhanced with increasing amplitudes and wavelength; (2) In the horizontal configuration, macrosegregation occurs in the center of the cavities and is enhanced with decreasing wavelength and increasing amplitude.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of macrosegregations in aluminum alloys solidified on uneven surfaces.
the effect of surface topography on solidification and macrosegregation.
the study of macrosegregations in aluminum alloys during solidification from uneven surfaces.

macrosegregation in aluminum alloys is a complex phenomenon, which depends not only on the surface topography but also on the solidification configuration.
